description: The bar chart illustrates the performance of a model across six different reasoning categories—“No Hallucination,” “Oriented,” “Active,” “Self-aware,” “Rigorous,” and “Correct”—by comparing the percentage of “Matched” (blue) and “Not Matched” (light gray) responses for each category. The horizontal axis represents the percentage scale from 0% to 100%, with tick marks at 20% intervals, while the vertical axis lists the six reasoning categories in descending order of “Matched” performance. In each category, a long blue bar indicates the high proportion of “Matched” responses, ranging from 94.00% (“Self-aware”) to 99.00% (“Correct”), while a short light gray bar to the right of each blue bar shows the corresponding “Not Matched” percentage, ranging from 1.00% (“Correct”) to 6.00% (“Self-aware”). The “No Hallucination” category shows a unique pattern, with a large blue bar at 98.33% “Matched” and a small gray bar at 1.67% “Not Matched,” but also includes a small gray bar embedded within the blue bar at approximately 40–50%, which may represent an internal subgroup or annotation not explained in the legend. The legend in the middle-right clarifies that blue corresponds to “Matched” and light gray to “Not Matched.” Overall, the chart visually emphasizes high accuracy across all categories, with “Correct” achieving near-perfect alignment and “Self-aware” showing the highest rate of mismatch.
